POST /v1/conversations.description: Makes a forum, private chat (dm), wall, note, project, event or folder. Every conversation is end-to-end encrypted: the creator makes the first conversation key on their device, seals a copy to each member device and sends those copies in `keys`. Creating a private chat that already exists answers 200 with the existing one. Who may create each kind depends on the role's rights (forum: Create forum, wall: Moderate posts, dm: Send private messages, project: Create project, ...). A wall's `audience` decides who is in it (a wall holds at most 5000 people).
POST /v1/conversations.access: any signed-in member of the organization (token issued with `org`)

request.kind: string, required. dm | forum | wall | note | ticket | project | event | folder
request.name: string. Required for forums, walls, projects and folders
request.privacy: string. open (anyone in the organization may join a forum) | invite
members: uuid. Person ids to add; you are added automatically
request.audience: string. Walls: org | sector | branch | unit | department
request.audience_ref: uuid. Walls: the unit the audience covers

keys.epoch: integer, required. Key generation this wrap is for
keys.wrapped_key: base64, required. The conversation key sealed to that device's public key

response.kind: string. dm | forum | wall | note | sharednote | ticket | project | event | folder
response.name: string. Forum, wall, project or folder name (absent for private chats)
response.epoch: integer. Current key generation; messages are sealed under it
response.my_role: string. owner | admin | member | viewer, my role in it (absent if not a member)
response.first_epoch: integer. The earliest key generation I can read
response.last_at: timestamp. When the latest message arrived
response.unread: integer. Messages I have not read
response.audience: string. Walls only: org | sector | branch | unit | department
response.audience_ref: uuid. Walls only: the structure unit the audience covers

errors.409: keys_incomplete: every member device needs a key; no_devices: set up secure messaging on this device first

POST /v1/conversations/{id}/messages.description: The message is sealed on the device: the sender picks the id (it is part of what the signature covers), chooses the key generation and sends the base64 envelope. The server checks that the sender may post here (forum posting rules, mute, role) and that the bytes look like an envelope; it cannot read the text. An `edit` is a new message of type `edit` whose `reply_to` is the original.
POST /v1/conversations/{id}/messages.access: any signed-in member of the organization (token issued with `org`)

request.id: uuid, required. Chosen by the sender: a time-ordered UUID v7 made from the device clock
request.epoch: integer, required. The key generation used
request.envelope: base64, required. Ciphertext plus signature, up to 512 KB
request.type: string, required. text | file | edit | ... 2-20 lowercase letters
request.reply_to: uuid. A message this replies to or edits

response.epoch: integer. Key generation it is sealed under
response.envelope: base64. Ciphertext plus the sender's signature; opened only on a member's device
response.type: string. text | file | edit | system ... chosen by the sender, 2-20 lowercase letters
response.reply_to: uuid. The message this answers (an `edit` points at the message it replaces)
response.deleted: boolean. true when removed; the envelope is then empty

errors.400: Not a valid envelope, unknown type, or the id is not a UUID v7 with a believable time
errors.403: posting_limited: the forum rules do not let you post here
errors.409: epoch_changed: the key changed, fetch the new key and send again; duplicate: that id was already sent

POST /v1/containers/{id}/records.summary: Add a record to a project, event, note or folder
POST /v1/containers/{id}/records.description: A record is one sealed item: a task, milestone, sprint, risk, standup, comment, calendar entry, RSVP or note. The server enforces who may write it and that the few plain `meta` fields are valid; the content stays sealed. Collections and their `meta`: task {column: backlog|todo|doing|review|done, due: date, assignee: uuid, sprint, priority: low|medium|high}, milestone {due, closed}, sprint {start, end, milestone}, risk {level: Low|Medium|High}, standup {day}, rsvp {going: boolean}, note {book: uuid, pinned: boolean}, entry {date, start, repeat, ...}.
POST /v1/containers/{id}/records.access: a member of the container, with the role's right for that collection (e.g. Edit tasks, Manage milestones, Add events)
